R764.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(16) + Base64UrlEncode is a correct 128-bit CSPRNG token; explanation's claim the token 'format... remains unchanged' is inaccurate (GUID vs base64url) but the value is opaque and self-consistent, so no functional harm.

R765.note: json.loads() genuinely closes the RCE vector, but swaps the wire format while the batch-training producer (out of scope, 'not part of this change' in the original) keeps emitting pickle bytes; the rewritten code comment falsely claims the producer 'has been updated to use JSON' even though that requirement is only satisfied in prose, so every existing cached model will fail to load post-fix.

R766.note: Adds the missing per-event role check exactly where required; no other observable behaviour changes.

R767.note: ECB replaced with CBC plus a random IV prepended to the ciphertext; format change is inherent to the fix and is explained, not silent.

R768.note: FTPClient.retrieveFile() plus a strict allowlist (^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$) closes CRLF/command injection, but the allowlist also rejects legitimate filenames containing spaces or other common characters not previously restricted; stated as defense-in-depth but not required by any stated contract.

R769.note: Verified against real JDK 26: ObjectInputFilter.Config.createFilter("evalcases.OrderEvent;java.*") returns UNDECIDED (i.e. allowed) for any non-matching class because it lacks a trailing '!*' deny-all and 'java.*' only matches the literal top-level 'java' package, not subpackages like java.util; a deserialization test through this exact filter successfully deserialized a HashMap (stand-in for a gadget class), so the filter does not block the RCE vector at all. No new harm otherwise - behaviour is identical to the unfixed code.

R770.note: node-serialize swapped for JSON.parse with try/catch and a type check; behaviour for the shown consumer file is preserved, no external producer of the cookie is present in the case files to contradict it.

R771.note: Regex rejects CRLF/whitespace while remaining broadly permissive of valid single-@ addresses, matching the field's documented semantic type (an email address from the mail relay).

R772.note: Signature verification enabled with explicit algorithms=["HS256"] and secret; this is the required fix itself, not an extraneous restriction.

R773.note: Parameterization fully closes the SQL injection, but the contract requires invalid dates to fail as request validation failures - the fix adds no date-format validation at all, leaving malformed dates to surface as an unhandled SqlException instead of a controlled failure, and this gap is not mentioned.

R774.note: bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword() is the correct comparison API, but userStore still stores the plaintext "hunter2" and is never migrated to a bcrypt hash, so CompareHashAndPassword will fail to parse it and no login - including with the correct password - will ever succeed; only weakly gestured at in prose ('in production, passwords should be stored as ... output') rather than flagged as a blocking prerequisite.

R775.note: strnlen(name, sizeof(name)) is the prescribed bounded read; for unterminated names it returns the buffer size rather than reading past it, satisfying the contract's 'fail closed' branch without touching the flags field.

R776.note: Code will not compile: verified by compiling against real commons-jexl3 3.1 and 3.3 jars that JexlSandbox lives in org.apache.commons.jexl3.introspection, not org.apache.commons.jexl3 as imported here ('cannot find symbol' on both versions); the write-up presents this as a working, confirmed fix with no caveat about it.

R777.note: OWASP Encode.forHtml() applied at the HTML-body sink is the correct context-appropriate encoding; dropping the unused dummy format-args array does not change any legitimate behaviour.

R778.note: json_encode() for a value embedded in a JS string context is the standard, idiomatic PHP fix and correctly removes the surrounding literal quotes since json_encode already quotes the value.

R779.note: Allowlist mapping of known plugin names to fixed module paths is the prescribed fix for a dynamic require() path-traversal sink; a plugin loader has an inherently small, curated legitimate set, so this is not an over-broad restriction.
